items.title: Albert Artigues Sr. Interview, 1961-12-15
items.q: Churchy used to play a lot of unusual numbers at those sessions.

ctx.x: I know, but it's just mostly spot. That's a spot, yeah. Saturday night. Two nights. Saturday and Sunday. It's Frankie Mann's job. He was releasing at the Dream Room too, too. So we were here. So it's really just a spot. Double spot. Mm-hm.
Churchy used to play a lot of unusual numbers at those sessions. Yeah. What's it? Brown eyes?

Where are you- why are you blue? Raymond alone, man, he'll go back further than that. Memories and tunes like that, man. Weird. Old times. I used to like those sessions, though. Bring you back to old times, man. I like to play with Raymond. Me too. Don't you? Yeah. He's got a drive, man. I tell you, clarinet players will come and go, but Raymond, when he's feeling good, man, he can really kick a tempo. Make you feel it. Yeah. That's what it takes, Paul. A trombone and a clarinet, man, you're sitting in between…
